resolutions.researcher_notes: Three distinct publishers agree the pipeline runs entirely within Nueces County, TX, matching both the sheet's StartPrefecture/District and EndPrefecture/District. (1) Natural Gas Intel (David Bradley, 'South Texas Expansion, Pomelo Connector Projects Granted FERC OK', Feb 15 2018): 'Pomelo Connector filed at FERC for permission to construct its 14-mile-long, 30-inch diameter pipeline in Texas connecting Tetco's Petronila Station in Nueces County to its Valley Crossing interconnect near Agua Dulce.' (2) Pipeline News / Pipeline & Gas Journal ('Ongoing Projects', Oct 2018 issue, PDF), project entry 'POMELO CONNECTOR LLC - (4/18)': 'Project: Pomelo Connector Pipeline ... Length: 14 miles, Diameter: 30 inches, Location: Nueces County, TX, Capacity: 400 MDth/d, Completion: 2018 -- Project will provide firm transportation capacity between Texas Eastern Transmission LP and the Nueces Header to be constructed by Valley Crossing Pipeline LLC.' (3) Canyon Midstream's own project page (owner of Pomelo Connector LLC) independently describes the project as a 14-mile, 30-inch pipeline in the same Nueces County corridor. Three distinct publishers (trade press outlet NGI, trade press outlet PGJ/Pipeline News, and the owner company) converging on the same county for both endpoints is high-tier, independent=true.

CONCERN: could not confirm a standalone $130,000,000 pipeline-construction cost for Pomelo, and found a materially different cost figure in the one primary source that discloses project economics. Spectra Energy Partners LP's Form 8-K (filed 2018-05-09, SEC EDGAR accession 0001144204-18-026689, Exhibit 99.1 earnings press release) states: 'In December 2017, SEP acquired Pomelo Connector LLC ... In April 2018, SEP commenced construction on the Pomelo Connector, a 14-mile pipeline that will provide 400,000 dth/d of natural gas to Valley Crossing ... The total project capex, including acquisition cost, is $260 million and is expected to be placed into service in the fourth quarter of 2018.' $260M (acquisition + construction, per SEP itself) does not match the sheet's $130M, and no source found breaks the figure down into a construction-only sub-total that would reconcile to $130M (it is plausible $130M is roughly half -- construction only, excluding the LLC acquisition price -- but that is my inference, not a sourced figure, so I am not proposing it as a ref). Checked and ruled out: the seed citation captioned '\"FERC approves $137M Enbridge project, Pomelo line to feed Mexico markets\"' (S&P Global, via Wayback capture http://web.archive.org/web/20240221075140/https://www.spglobal.com/marketintelligence/en/news-insights/trending/o1-ndp_bh6ywlrlqblwqta2) -- read the full article body, not just the headline, and the $137.3 million figure it reports is explicitly attributed to the companion South Texas Expansion Project (STEP)/Texas Eastern Transmission compressor-and-facilities project, not to Pomelo; the article does not state a separate Pomelo-only cost. Also checked: the Oct-2018 Pipeline News 'Ongoing Projects' PDF entry for Pomelo Connector LLC (has Length/Diameter/Location/Capacity/Completion fields) carries no cost field at all. EIA's generic 'Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects' page (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php) is a navigation/data-portal surface, not a document, and was not usable as a citation per the brief's rule against citing navigation surfaces even after locating the underlying dataset page. No FERC certificate order text (CP17-19) was accessible via elibrary.ferc.gov in this session to check for a stated project cost. Declining to propose a ref for $130,000,000; flagging the $260M SEP figure (which describes a superset -- acquisition + construction) for Update to reconcile.

CONCERN: two independent sources point to a 2018 target/completion rather than the sheet's StartYear1=2019, and neither is a confirmed ACTUAL in-service date, so I am not proposing a ref for either year. Spectra Energy Partners' 8-K exhibit (SEC EDGAR, filed 2018-05-09, cited above) states the Pomelo Connector 'is expected to be placed into service in the fourth quarter of 2018.' Independently, Pipeline News' Oct-2018 'Ongoing Projects' PDF lists the Pomelo Connector LLC project's 'Completion: 2018.' Both are dated mid/late 2018 and describe an EXPECTED/near-term completion, not a confirmed later in-service event, so they could simply predate a subsequent slip into 2019 -- consistent with, not necessarily contradicting, the sheet. Working the other direction: FERC's original construction certificate for the related South Texas Expansion Project set a service deadline of Feb. 15, 2020 (per the S&P Global Wayback capture: 'FERC said the projects must be ready for service by Feb. 15, 2020'), which read alone would suggest a later actual date, but that deadline text describes the regulatory backstop, not Pomelo's actual completion, and Pomelo (per the same 8-K) had already started construction in April 2018 aiming for Q4 2018. Checked and ruled out: SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Pomelo Connector' as an exact phrase surfaces only Enbridge/Spectra Energy Partners corporate filings (10-Ks, 8-Ks, S-4/425 merger filings) that name the project in passing without giving an actual in-service date distinct from the Q4 2018 target already found; a broader search on the bare word 'Pomelo' returns only unrelated 'Pomelo Domestic/Offshore Fund' investment-vehicle Form D filings, not the pipeline. Natural Gas Intel's Feb-2018 FERC-certificate article and the Federal Register/Casetext environmental-review notices (seed citations) predate construction and give no completion date. No source found confirming an actual 2019 in-service date, and two sources point toward a 2018 target instead -- flagging the tension for Update rather than citing either year.
